blocks.title: Today’s Learning Roadmap
content: sketch angles in standard position
find coterminal and reference angles in degrees and radians

blocks.title: Predict: sketch angles in standard position
content: Where does a negative angle rotate, and what never changes about standard position?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: sketch angles in standard position
content: The initial side lies on the positive x-axis.
Positive rotation is counterclockwise; negative rotation is clockwise.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of standard-position.svg.

assets.alt: Coordinate axes with Quadrants I through IV. The vertex is at the origin and the initial side lies on the positive x-axis. An orange arc rotates counterclockwise to a terminal side in Quadrant II, labeled positive. A purple arc rotates clockwise to a terminal side in Quadrant IV, labeled negative.
assets.caption: Start on the positive x-axis; the sign sets the direction.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: sketch angles in standard position
content: Sketch $225^\circ$ and $-120^\circ$ and identify their quadrants.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of standard-model.svg.
steps: $225^\circ=180^\circ+45^\circ$, so it terminates in Quadrant III.
Both begin on the positive x-axis; rotation direction distinguishes the sketches.

assets.alt: Two sets of axes. On the left, an orange counterclockwise arc of 225 degrees ends in Quadrant III, 45 degrees past the negative x-axis. On the right, a purple clockwise arc of negative 120 degrees also ends in Quadrant III. Both begin on the positive x-axis.
assets.caption: Both angles end in Quadrant III.

blocks.title: You Try: sketch angles in standard position
content: Sketch 310° and label initial and terminal sides.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of standard-practice.svg.
answer: The initial side is the positive x-axis; $310^\circ$ terminates in Quadrant IV, $50^\circ$ below the positive x-axis.

assets.alt: Empty coordinate axes with Quadrants I through IV and the quarter-turn marks 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees. The initial side is drawn on the positive x-axis. No terminal side is drawn.
assets.caption: Start on the initial side and rotate counterclockwise.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: sketch angles in standard position
content: Do not measure from the y-axis.
Quadrant boundaries are not inside a quadrant.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: sketch angles in standard position
content: Describe standard position without drawing it.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Predict: find coterminal and reference angles in degrees and radians
content: How can infinitely many angles share one terminal side?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: find coterminal and reference angles in degrees and radians
content: Coterminal angles differ by $360^\circ k$ or $2\pi k$.
Reduce large magnitudes before locating the terminal side.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of coterminal.svg.

assets.alt: One terminal side in Quadrant I at 45 degrees. A short orange arc shows 45 degrees. A blue spiral shows 405 degrees, one full turn more. A purple clockwise arc shows negative 315 degrees, one full turn less. All three end on the same terminal side.
assets.caption: Full turns change the angle, not the terminal side.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: find coterminal and reference angles in degrees and radians
content: Find positive and negative coterminal angles for $-97^\circ$ and $9\pi/7$.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of coterminal-model.svg.
steps: Coterminal angles differ by full rotations.

assets.alt: A terminal side in Quadrant III just past the negative y-axis. A purple clockwise arc measures negative 97 degrees and a larger orange counterclockwise arc measures 263 degrees. Both end on the same terminal side.
assets.caption: One terminal side, two directions of rotation.

blocks.title: You Try: find coterminal and reference angles in degrees and radians
content: Find a coterminal angle between 0° and 360° for 765°.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: find coterminal and reference angles in degrees and radians
content: Add or subtract full rotations only.
Keep degree and radian units separate.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: find coterminal and reference angles in degrees and radians
content: Give the general coterminal-angle formulas.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Predict: use radians to compute arc length
content: What does one radian measure geometrically?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: use radians to compute arc length
content: Arc length is $s=r\theta$ when $\theta$ is in radians.
Radians connect central angle directly to distance.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of arc-length.svg.

assets.alt: A circle of radius r with a shaded sector. The central angle theta is between two radii, and the orange arc s lies opposite it. The caption reads s equals r theta, theta in radians.
assets.caption: The arc s sits opposite the central angle θ.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: use radians to compute arc length
content: For $r=12$ and $\theta=2\pi/3$, compute arc length.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of arc-model.svg.
steps: The angle is already in radians.
$8\pi$ is about 25.133 units, less than the full circumference $24\pi$.

assets.alt: A circle with radius 12 and a shaded sector with central angle two pi over three radians, one third of the circle. The orange arc s lies opposite the angle.
assets.caption: Two thirds of π is one third of a full turn.

blocks.title: You Try: use radians to compute arc length
content: Find s for $r=8$ and $\theta=135^\circ$.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of arc-practice.svg.

assets.alt: A circle with radius 8 and a shaded sector with central angle 135 degrees. The arc opposite the angle is labeled s equals question mark.
assets.caption: Convert 135° to radians before using s = rθ.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: use radians to compute arc length
content: Convert degrees before using $s=r\theta$.
Arc length has linear units.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: use radians to compute arc length
content: Explain why radians make $s=r\theta$ dimensionally natural.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Predict: use right-triangle trigonometric ratios
content: Which two sides define sine, cosine, and tangent relative to an angle?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of ratio-sides.svg.

assets.alt: A right triangle with angle theta at the lower left. The blue bottom leg touching theta is the adjacent side. The teal vertical leg across from theta is the opposite side. The orange side across from the right angle is the hypotenuse.
assets.caption: Each side is named from the angle θ.

blocks.title: use right-triangle trigonometric ratios
content: SOH-CAH-TOA selects the ratio.
Reciprocal functions invert sine, cosine, and tangent.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of ratio-definitions.svg.

assets.alt: A right triangle with angle theta, colored sides adjacent in blue, opposite in teal and hypotenuse in orange. Below it, sine is opposite over hypotenuse, cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, tangent is opposite over adjacent. The reciprocals cosecant, secant and cotangent flip each fraction.
assets.caption: Colors match each side to its place in the ratios.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: use right-triangle trigonometric ratios
content: A right triangle has opposite leg 40, adjacent leg 9, and hypotenuse 41. Find all six ratios.
verification: Verify all right-triangle ratios and calculator values.
Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of ratio-model.svg.

assets.alt: A tall right triangle drawn to scale. Angle theta is at the lower left. The adjacent leg is 9, the opposite leg is 40, and the hypotenuse is 41. A note checks that 9 squared plus 40 squared equals 41 squared.
assets.caption: Drawn to scale: 9, 40, 41.

blocks.title: Exact values from the special triangles
content: $\sin30^\circ=\tfrac{1}{2}$, $\cos30^\circ=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, $\tan30^\circ=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{3}$
$\sin45^\circ=\cos45^\circ=\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$, $\tan45^\circ=1$
$\sin60^\circ=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, $\cos60^\circ=\tfrac{1}{2}$, $\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$
Keep exact values unless a decimal is asked for, and round only the final answer.
instructor_notes: Read each value from the triangle on the right; students should be able to redraw both triangles from memory before Quiz 10.
verification: Verify the nine exact values against the 1-1-√2 and 1-√3-2 triangles.
Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of special-triangles.svg.

assets.alt: A 45-45-90 triangle with legs 1 and 1 and hypotenuse root 2. A 30-60-90 triangle with the short leg 1 opposite 30 degrees, the long leg root 3 opposite 60 degrees, and hypotenuse 2. Both are drawn to scale.
assets.caption: Exact side ratios for the two special triangles.

blocks.title: You Try: use right-triangle trigonometric ratios
content: Given $\sin\theta=\tfrac{5}{6}$ for an acute angle $\theta$, sketch the triangle, find the third side, and give the other five ratios as exact values.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.
verification: Verify sqrt(11) and the five exact ratios.
Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of one-ratio.svg.

assets.alt: A right triangle drawn to scale with angle theta at the lower left, the side opposite theta equal to 5, the hypotenuse equal to 6, and the adjacent side marked with a question mark. A note reads sine theta equals 5 over 6.
assets.caption: Givens only: find the third side first.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: use right-triangle trigonometric ratios
content: Opposite and adjacent depend on the chosen reference angle.
Keep the calculator in the requested angle mode.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify all right-triangle ratios and calculator values.
Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of ratio-swap.svg.

assets.alt: The same right triangle drawn twice. Measured from angle A at the lower left, the bottom leg is adjacent and the vertical leg is opposite. Measured from angle B at the top, the bottom leg is opposite and the vertical leg is adjacent. The hypotenuse does not change.
assets.caption: Change the angle and opposite and adjacent trade places.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: use right-triangle trigonometric ratios
content: Write the ratio-selection rule you will use under time pressure.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of sin-cos-graph.svg.
blocks.pacing_checkpoint: Check elapsed time before beginning the next objective.

assets.alt: A graph from 0 to 90 degrees. Sine rises from 0 to 1 and cosine falls from 1 to 0. They cross at 45 degrees, where both are about 0.7071. Both stay between 0 and 1 for acute angles.
assets.caption: For acute angles, sine and cosine stay between 0 and 1.

blocks.title: Predict: choose the ratio for a word problem
content: You know the hypotenuse and want the side opposite the angle. Which ratio do you use, and do you multiply or divide?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: Choose the ratio from the side you know and the side you want
content: Use the ratio that contains the side you know and the side you want.
If the unknown is on top of the fraction, multiply; if it is on the bottom, divide.
To find an angle, use inverse trig: $A=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}\right)$.
To solve a right triangle, find all three missing parts, then check the angle sum and the Pythagorean theorem.
verification: Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of choose-ratio.svg.

assets.alt: A right triangle with angle theta and its sides colored: adjacent blue, opposite teal, hypotenuse orange. A table pairs the two sides in a problem with a ratio: hypotenuse and opposite use sine, hypotenuse and adjacent use cosine, adjacent and opposite use tangent. Below: if the unknown is in the numerator, multiply; if it is in the denominator, divide.
assets.caption: Pick the ratio from the two sides in the problem.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: solve a right triangle
content: Solve right triangle $ABC$ with $C=90^\circ$, $a=150$ and $c=345$: find $b$, $A$ and $B$.
verification: Verify A ≈ 25.8°, B ≈ 64.2°, b ≈ 310.7 (Prof. Young lists b = 311, A = 25.8°).
Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of solve-triangle.svg.

assets.alt: Right triangle ABC with the right angle at C. Side a, opposite A, is 150; the hypotenuse c is 345. Side b and angles A and B are unknown. Drawn to scale.
assets.caption: Drawn to scale. Find the side b and both acute angles.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: two right triangles, one height
content: From one point the angle of elevation to the top of a tower is $40^\circ$. From a point 50 ft closer it is $55^\circ$. Find the height $h$.
verification: Verify the two-triangle calculation (d about 71.23 ft, h about 101.72 ft).
Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of two-triangles.svg.
steps: Set them equal and solve: $d=\dfrac{50\tan40^\circ}{\tan55^\circ-\tan40^\circ}\approx71.23$ ft.

assets.alt: A tower of height h. From a far point the angle of elevation is 40 degrees; from a point 50 feet closer it is 55 degrees. The near point is d feet from the base. Both triangles share the height h. Drawn to scale.
assets.caption: Drawn to scale. Both triangles share the height h.

blocks.title: You Try: an unknown in the denominator
content: A ramp must rise 2 ft, and it makes a 10° angle with the ground. How long is the ramp?
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.
verification: Verify the ramp calculation (about 11.52 ft).
Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of ramp.svg.

assets.alt: A long, low right triangle drawn to scale. The ramp is the hypotenuse, marked with a question mark. It makes a 10 degree angle with the ground and rises 2 feet.
assets.caption: The ramp is the hypotenuse; 2 ft is opposite the 10° angle.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: right-triangle word problems
content: A leg must be shorter than the hypotenuse.
Degree mode, and parentheses for inverse trig: $\sin^{-1}(5.5\div6.5)$, not $\sin^{-1}5.5\div6.5$.
In two-triangle problems, keep $d$ and $d+50$ with the right angles, and round only at the end.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify special-triangle and word-problem calculations.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: right-triangle word problems
content: List the steps to solve a right triangle and the two checks you finish with.

blocks.title: Session Summary and Exit Ticket
content: State the most important idea from today without looking at your notes.
Complete one representative setup and identify the step most likely to cause an error.
Write one question that should be answered before the next assessment.
